findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, making the regression test racy and unreliable
findings.body: `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` starts a background thread that records exceptions into `caughtExceptions`, then sets `deletedAll` and immediately asserts the list is empty without ever joining the thread. Consequences: (a) an exception raised by the in-flight request (exactly the NPE this PR fixes) can be appended after the assertion has already run, so the test can pass even when the bug is present — the regression coverage is illusory; (b) if the thread has not yet issued a single request before the deletions complete, nothing is exercised at all. The thread reference should be kept, `Thread.join()` (with timeout) called before asserting, and the test should also assert that at least one read actually completed.

findings.title: Background thread can spin forever if group deletion throws
findings.body: `deletedAll.set(true)` (line 155) is only reached if every `groups().group(groupUuid).remove()` call succeeds. If any delete throws (e.g. 404/500 during the concurrent read load), the exception propagates out of the test method and `deletedAll` is never set, leaving the started non-daemon thread looping and continuously issuing admin REST calls. That hangs the surefire JVM / build instead of failing cleanly. Set the flag in a `finally` block (and/or create the thread as a daemon).

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount() now returns null, moving the NPE to callers
findings.body: The fix changes `getSubGroupsCount()` to return `null` when the group no longer exists in the store. `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` returns a boxed `Long` that callers routinely use in arithmetic/comparisons or propagate into `GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(...)` (see `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`). Any caller performing auto-unboxing (`getSubGroupsCount() > 0`) will now throw an NPE instead, and the admin REST response will contain a null/absent `subGroupCount`, which the admin console uses to decide whether a group is expandable. Returning `0L` for a group that has been concurrently removed keeps the contract non-null and avoids simply relocating the NPE.

findings.title: Unthrottled busy loop requesting Integer.MAX_VALUE groups
findings.body: The reader thread calls `groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` in a tight loop with no sleep. Each iteration asks the server for an unbounded page of groups, so the test saturates a CPU core and floods the server with large queries for the whole duration of the delete loop, slowing the test suite and increasing the chance of unrelated timeouts. Add a small sleep and a realistic page size.
